checkpoints.description: [milestone 1/6] Wave 0 of the engine-depth plan: the gaps are now machine-runnable rather than prose. Added tests/integration/engine-gaps.test.ts (13 tests: 6 pass, 7 it.fails pinning verified gaps), scripts/engine-gaps.ts (npm run engine:gaps) and a frozen evals/results/baselines/engine-baseline-v1.json. Re-verification corrected plan v1 twice: CRLF/BOM preservation already works end to end and is NOT a gap, and the missing tool history is deeper than a mapper bug because appendMessage only accepts user|assistant so tool results never enter the message store. 624 tests pass, typecheck and lint clean.

[1/6] Engine-depth plan: pin each verified gap, then close them wave by wave. Waves: (0) failing-fast tests + measured baseline, done in this commit; (1) derive the compaction budget from the model window, add an LLM summariser with mechanical fallback, re-inject an artifact manifest, and give the message store a tool role so a resumed run sees its tool results; (2) edit-match cascade for indentation and CRLF/LF, plus a read ledger with stale-write refusal reusing the FILE_CONFLICT pattern; (3) parallel read batches and real background shells; (4) per-step retry and a normalised doom-loop signature; (5) CLI parity (-p, --model, stdin, --no-session, -r, finer exit codes). CRLF/BOM serialisation is already correct and is excluded.

impact_assessment.why: The engine cannot hold a real repository in context (24k compaction against a 200k-1M window), cannot heal ordinary model drift in edits, can clobber a file it never read, and forgets its own tool results on resume. These are the gaps that stop real work completing; tool breadth and UI are not the constraint.
impact_assessment.benefits: A run can use the window the model actually has, a resumed run keeps its tool history, edits stop being refused over whitespace, and an unread or externally changed file cannot be silently overwritten.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: data-testid, exit codes and docs/FEATURES.md are pinned claims; dependency: none added; concurrency: parallel reads share the effect ledger and approval prompts; state: a model-backed summariser adds a provider call that costs tokens and can fail, and a message-store role change needs a schema migration
impact_assessment.mitigation: Summariser failure degrades to the mechanical path rather than blocking a run; the schema change is additive with a version bump; parallel execution is restricted to read-only batches; every wave is re-measured against engine-baseline-v1.json and a wave with no paired numbers is not counted as done

checkpoints.description: [milestone 2/6] Waves 1 and 2 landed. (1) Context: HarnessProfile.contextTokens is now optional and a live run derives its budget from the model window via budgetForModel (192000 for a 200k-window model instead of a hardcoded 24000, 0.12 -> 0.96 of the window), ChatRequest.maxTokens is populated from the catalog maxOutput (it was declared and never set), compaction prefers a model summary with the mechanical one as fallback, and the compacted head names offloaded artifact paths so they can be re-read. (2) Edit/write correctness: edits.ts matches the exact substring first then heals CRLF/LF, trailing-whitespace or indentation drift over whole-line windows and reports the strategy; server/readLedger.ts refuses a full overwrite of a file this run has not read or that changed since, and refuses a targeted edit of a file that changed since (its oldString already pins the content). Schema 10 adds the tool-turn columns. 632 tests pass, typecheck and lint clean, 11/12 gates; agent-perf and agent-bench fail only under machine load and pass at 3.49 ms and 106.8 ms on a quiet run, both at or below their recorded baselines.

[milestone 3/6] Wave 4 landed: a transient model step is now retried up to three times with jittered backoff instead of blocking the run, while a deterministic fixture or replayed step is never retried (that would shift eval responses). Each attempt is a provider.retry event. 634 tests pass.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Two follow-ups from re-verifying my own proposals: (1) the perf recorder measured one process and called it a baseline, so a recording is now 5 passes reduced to a median plus MAD and a gate run is 3 passes, with a metric failing only past 1.5x AND median+6 MADs; commitP95 budget raised 5 -> 10 ms on instruction. (2) A resumed run could not see its tool results: appendMessage now accepts a tool role written without a text.ended event, listMessages excludes tool rows unless asked, and rebuildMessages carries them through.

impact_assessment.why: The perf baseline described a different host (pristine tree failed it too) and a resumed conversation repeated work it had already done, so neither number nor behaviour could be trusted.
impact_assessment.benefits: A timing claim now comes with its spread, so a busy machine is visible instead of silently failing; and work resumed in a conversation continues instead of restarting blind.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: agent-perf baseline schema 1 -> 2, and listMessages default shape; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: tool rows are durable state the UI does not render
impact_assessment.mitigation: A schema-1 baseline still reads through its metrics key; tool rows are excluded by default so every existing reader is byte-for-byte unchanged; both proven by the 638-test suite and 12/12 gates

checkpoints.description: [milestone 2/2] Done and verified: 638 tests pass with zero it.fails left in engine-gaps.test.ts, and 12/12 gates are green. A/B with one recorder against both trees in a linked worktree at 8336b54 shows the pre-change tree is not faster (toolDispatchP95 7.68 vs 6.39, agentRunP95 41.11 vs 33.77), so the old 5 ms budget was describing a host this code no longer runs on. Perf gates measured alone pass with tight spread (agentRunP95 MAD 0.73 ms); when the gate runs alongside the whole suite the MAD blows up to 31.99 ms on a 58 ms median, which is exactly the interference the spread now makes visible.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Fix the measured prompt-test flake: the test asserted a bare 'L5' against a prompt that embeds a mkdtemp path whose random suffix contains L5 in 0.4% of samples, so it failed about once in 250 full-suite runs for a reason unrelated to imports. Both assertions now name the whole line.

impact_assessment.why: A gate that fails at random teaches everyone to re-run it rather than read it, which is worse than the bug it hides.
impact_assessment.benefits: The prompt test now fails only when the import depth behaviour actually changes.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the assertion is stricter, not looser; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH is 3 and verified, so 'L3 inlined, its own @l4 plain' remains the behaviour under test; the full suite is green.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Wave 3b: server/shellTasks.ts gives bash a real background mode. run_in_background starts a detached child, writes its output to a log under the state home, and returns a task id and log path; shell_output, shell_tasks and kill_shell read, list and stop it. The pre-existing killProcessTree teardown is reused, every task dies with the server, and a 30-minute lifetime bounds a task nobody stops.

impact_assessment.why: Every command blocked the agent loop, so a build or a watch occupied a whole step and the delegate tool's background flag was declared but never read.
impact_assessment.benefits: A long command no longer costs the run its remaining steps, and its output lands in a file the agent can read a window of instead of flooding the context.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: three new tool names enter the harness profile; dependency: none; concurrency: a registry shared across runs in one process; state: log files under the state home
impact_assessment.mitigation: The registry is capped at 40 tasks, every task is killed on server stop, kill reuses the tested process-tree teardown, and 6 tests drive start/read/offset/list/kill/refusal

checkpoints.description: [milestone 1/1] Verified: 6 new background-task tests pass, the full suite is 116 files green, and all 12 gates pass on a quiet host. The delegate tool's previously-dead background flag is left alone: making it real means a detached sub-agent, which is a separate change from a detached shell.
